ov: A slender, fast antelope of the dry south-west of Africa, with a white face, a dark stripe from eye to mouth and a reddish-brown band along each flank. It lives in herds, feeds mainly at dawn and dusk, and is the national animal of South Africa.

why.et: Hunted as game and farmed; springbok meat is sold in South African supermarkets and exported.

rg: South and south-west Africa: north-west South Africa, the Kalahari, Namibia, Botswana and south-west Angola.
df: Shrubs and succulents, plus grasses when green. It gets its water from juicy plants and can go without drinking for years.
fx: In extreme cases a springbok may never drink water in its whole life, eating flowers, seeds and leaves before dawn when they are juiciest.
notes: RESOLVED (owner approved all suggestions, including the optional ones, 2026-09-29; ac left unchanged for eland, springbok and muntjac): The fact is confirmed: pronking is "multiple leaps into the air, up to 2 m ... with the back bowed", and the name is Afrikaans spring ("jump") and bok ("buck"). lf 7–10 fits "up to 10 years in the wild".
